source.title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum

accepted.question_text: Let λ be an infinite cardinal, let I be a set with |I| = λ, and let D be a regular ultrafilter on I. For the ultrapower (ω,<)^I/D of the usual linear order on the natural numbers, define C(D) to be the set of pairs (κ1,κ2) such that κ1 and κ2 are infinite regular cardinals, κ1 + κ2 ≤ |I|, and (ω,<)^I/D has a (κ1,κ2)-cut: a strictly increasing sequence of cofinality κ1 and a strictly decreasing sequence of cofinality κ2 with all left-side elements below all right-side elements and with no element of the ultrapower lying strictly between the two sequences. Which sets can occur as C(D) for regular ultrafilters D?

evidence.quote: General Problem 1.1 ... determine the possible values of C(D) = {(κ1, κ2) : κ1, κ2 are infinite and regular ...}
We say the set has a (κ1, κ2)-cut if ... there is no c such that ... aα < c < bβ.

accepted.question_text: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on I, and let C(D) be the cut spectrum of (ω,<)^I/D. Suppose C(D) is nonempty and κ ≤ |I| is the least regular cardinal for which the symmetric cut (κ,κ) belongs to C(D). For which cardinals μ < κ can the asymmetric cut (κ,μ) also belong to C(D)?
accepted.context_brief: Asymmetric cuts at the first symmetric cut

accepted.question_text: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on I, and let C(D) be the set of all pairs of infinite regular cardinals (κ1,κ2) whose corresponding unfilled cuts occur in (ω,<)^I/D. If (κ1,κ2) belongs to C(D), must the symmetric cut (κ1 + κ2, κ1 + κ2) also belong to C(D)?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.11. Suppose (κ1, κ2) ∈ C(D). Is (κ1 + κ2, κ1 + κ2) ∈ C(D)?

accepted.question_text: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on I with |I| = λ. Let κ1 and κ2 be infinite regular cardinals with λ ≤ κ1 + κ2 < 2^λ, and suppose the ultrapower (ω,<)^I/D has a (κ1,κ2)-cut. If κ = κ1 + κ2, must there be some tree T, in the sense of a partially ordered set whose predecessors of any node are well ordered, such that the ultrapower T^λ/D contains a strictly increasing κ-indexed sequence with no upper bound?
accepted.context_brief: Cuts and unbounded paths through trees

evidence.quote: By a tree we will mean a partially ordered set in which the set of predecessors of any given node is well ordered.

accepted.question_text: For a regular ultrafilter D on I with λ = |I|, say that D has uniqueness for a regular cardinal κ when any two cuts in C(D) with left cofinality κ have the same right cofinality: if (κ,θ) and (κ,θ') both belong to C(D), then θ = θ'. What are necessary and sufficient conditions on D ensuring that D has uniqueness for every regular κ ≤ λ?
accepted.context_brief: Uniqueness of cuts in cut spectra

accepted.question_text: Let p denote the first cardinal κ for which Martin's axiom MA_κ for σ-centered partial orders fails. For weaker saturation notions than the one captured by p, especially those corresponding to combinatorially natural first-order theories such as T_feq, the theory of an existentially closed model of a parametrized family of independent equivalence relations, and T_{3,2}, the theory of the generic tetrahedron-free three-hypergraph, do these weaker notions give rise to natural and interesting cardinal invariants?
accepted.context_brief: Cardinal invariants from weaker saturation notions

evidence.quote: p is the first cardinal κ for which MAκ(σ-centered) fails
There are natural weaker notions corresponding to saturation of some combinatorially natural theories, such as Tfeq ...
Do these weaker notions give rise to natural and interesting cardinal invariants?

accepted.question_text: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on I with |I| ≥ λ, and let N = ω^I/D. Suppose D admits internal maps between sets of size λ, meaning that for any two λ-indexed sequences of distinct elements of N there is an internal bijection h:N → N sending the ith element of the first sequence to the ith element of the second sequence for every i < λ. Must it follow that for any two strictly increasing λ-indexed sequences in N, there is an internal order-preserving partial function h, with domain and range contained in N, sending each element of the first sequence to the corresponding element of the second sequence?
accepted.context_brief: Internal maps versus order-preserving internal maps

accepted.question_text: Let D be a regular ultrafilter. If D is good for equality, must C(D) be empty? Equivalently, must D be good, where good means |I|^+-good: every monotonic function from finite subsets of |I| into D has a multiplicative refinement? Equivalently, if D admits internal maps between small sets in the sense captured by good-for-equality, must D also admit internal order-preserving maps between small increasing sequences?
accepted.context_brief: Good for equality versus good ultrafilters

evidence.quote: Say that D is good if it is |I|+-good.
General Problem 3.5. Let D be a regular ultrafilter. If D is good for equality, is C(D) = ∅?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist regular ultrafilters that are λ^+-OK but not λ^+-good? Here λ^+-OK is the weakening of λ^+-good obtained by requiring multiplicative refinements only for monotone functions f:[λ]^{<ℵ0} → D such that f(u) depends only on the size of the finite set u.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.6 (Dow 1985 [3]). Do there exist regular ultrafilters which are λ+-OK but not λ+-good?
the definition of λ-OK is a weakening of λ+-good which requires multiplicative refinements ...

accepted.question_text: Let D be a filter on the natural numbers containing the cofinite sets. A weakly peculiar (δ,θ)-D-cut in ω^ω consists of functions f_α for α < δ and g_β for β < θ such that the f_α sequence is increasing modulo D, the g_β sequence is decreasing modulo D, every f_α is below every g_β modulo D, and no function f can fill the cut after strengthening D by any D-positive set. Let spec_uq be the set of regular cardinals κ satisfying uniqueness for such cuts: if there are weakly peculiar cuts of left cofinality κ and right cofinalities θ0 and θ1, then θ0 = θ1. Let spec_uqm be the analogous spectrum in which the uniqueness is witnessed by an internal order-preserving partial map between the corresponding sequences. Are these two spectra equal? At minimum, are the cardinal invariants derived from these spectra equal?

evidence.quote: Definition 2.3 ... specuq = {κ : ... θ1 = θ2}.
Problem 3.7. Is specuq = specuqm? At least, are the derived cardinal invariants equal?

accepted.question_text: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on λ. Give an internal set-theoretic characterization of a family F of monotonic functions from [λ]^{<ℵ0} to D that is minimal, in an appropriate sense, for the following property: if every f in F has a multiplicative refinement, then D is good.

evidence.quote: General Problem 4.3. Give an internal set-theoretic characterization of a family F ...

accepted.question_text: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on λ, let μ be sufficiently large, and form the ultrapower N = (H(μ),∈)^λ/D, where H(μ) denotes the sets hereditarily of cardinality less than μ. Suppose N is λ^+-saturated for functions, meaning that every partial function from N to N whose domain has cardinality at most λ is extended by some internal function. Must D be good?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4. Suppose D is a regular ultrafilter on λ such that N = (H(µ), ǫ)^λ/D ...

trace.notes: The original zbMATH URL was blocked by a Cloudflare challenge in local curl. An existing local resolver index identified zbMATH document 6767146 as 'Open problems on ultrafilters and some connections to the continuum' with DOI 10.1090/conm/690/13866. Exact-title web recovery found the author-posted PDF at the resolved locator.

Mapped PDF structure: title/abstract; Section 1 The cut spectrum; Section 2 A uniqueness theorem; Section 3 On internal maps; Section 4 Bases for goodness; Appendix; References. Likely open-problem regions were labeled General Problem 1.1, Problems 1.10-1.16, Problems 3.4-3.7, General Problem 4.3, and Problem 4.4, with one footnoted Keisler-order question.
Extracted cut-spectrum candidates q_001 through q_006 and the footnoted Keisler-order candidate q_014 from Section 1.
Extracted q_007, an explicit question about weaker saturation notions and cardinal invariants, from the discussion following Theorem 2.4.
Extracted internal-map and ultrafilter-construction candidates q_008 through q_011 from Section 3.
Extracted bases-for-goodness candidates q_012 and q_013 from Section 4.
Expanded C(D), regular ultrafilter context, and the definition of a cut into the question text.
Restated the first-symmetric-cut assumption and asymmetric-cut question without relying on prior notation.
Restated the symmetric-sum cut problem using the definition of C(D).
Included the tree definition and the ultrapower/unbounded-path condition.
Expanded the uniqueness definition before asking for necessary and sufficient conditions.
